Read a BDHS recode file from your data store

Source: R/read.R
bdhs_read.Rd

Loads any round and recode you have imported with bdhs_import() in one line. Only the requested columns are read from disk, which makes reading a few variables from even the largest files fast.

Usage

bdhs_read(
  survey,
  recode,
  vars = NULL,
  vars_regex = NULL,
  indicators = NULL,
  keep_design = TRUE,
  labels = c("haven", "factor", "codes"),
  n_max = Inf
)

Arguments

survey

A survey reference understood by bdhs_survey_id(), e.g. 2022, "2017-18" or "BD2014DHS".

recode

A recode code (see bdhs_recodes()), e.g. "IR" or "KR".

vars

Variables to read (case-insensitive). NULL reads all of them unless vars_regex is given. Requested variables that do not exist in the file are skipped with a warning.

vars_regex

Regular expressions; variables whose (lower-case) names match any of them are read too.

indicators

Indicator ids from bdhs_indicator_list(). Every variable these indicators need is read, so the result can go straight into bdhs_estimate(). Combines with vars and vars_regex.

keep_design

If TRUE (default) and variables are selected, also read the identifiers, survey design variables and interview dates needed to link files, detect the round and build a survey design with bdhs_design(): caseid, hhid, hvidx, bidx, midx, v000-v003, v005, v007, v008, v021-v025 (and their hv/mv equivalents), the child's birth date and age (b3, b19) and the all-woman factors awfact*.

labels

How to return labelled variables: "haven" (default) keeps haven::labelled() columns; "factor" converts every variable whose values are all labelled to a factor with haven::as_factor() (levels = "labels"), leaving partially labelled variables such as z-scores with flag codes as labelled numbers; "codes" drops value labels (keeping variable labels) and turns extended missing values into plain NA.

n_max

Maximum number of rows to read.

Value

A tibble with the attributes bdhs_survey_id, bdhs_recode and bdhs_file (the DHS file stem, e.g. "BDIR81FL").

Details

Column names are returned in lower case. Variable labels and value labels are kept as haven::labelled() columns by default, and Stata extended missing values (.a to .z) as tagged NAs.

See also

bdhs_read_file() to read a file that is not in the store, bdhs_inventory() to see what you have.

Other data store: bdhs_data_dir(), bdhs_download(), bdhs_forget(), bdhs_identify_file(), bdhs_import(), bdhs_inventory(), bdhs_read_file(), bdhs_sitrep()

Examples

# Synthetic data written under a DHS file name, for illustration only
f <- file.path(tempdir(), "BDIR81FL.DTA")
haven::write_dta(bdhs_simulate(2022, "IR", n_clusters = 6, households = 4), f)
bdhs_import(f, format = "dta", quiet = TRUE)

ir <- bdhs_read(2022, "IR", vars = c("v012", "v106"))
names(ir)
#>  [1] "caseid"  "v000"    "v001"    "v002"    "v005"    "v003"    "v007"   
#>  [8] "v021"    "v022"    "v023"    "v024"    "v025"    "v008"    "v012"   
#> [15] "v106"    "awfactt" "awfactu" "awfactr" "awfacte" "awfactw"

# Exactly the columns two indicators need
ir <- bdhs_read(2022, "IR", indicators = c("fp_cpr_modern", "fp_unmet_total"))
bdhs_estimate(ir, c("fp_cpr_modern", "fp_unmet_total"))
#> # BDHS estimates: 2 indicators | BD2022DHS | 95% CI
#> # A tibble: 2 × 10
#>   survey_id indicator      label      estimate    se ci_low ci_high n_unweighted
#>   <chr>     <chr>          <chr>         <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>        <int>
#> 1 BD2022DHS fp_cpr_modern  Contracep…    48.0  11.1  18.3      79.1           19
#> 2 BD2022DHS fp_unmet_total Unmet nee…     3.86  4.13  0.115    58.3           19
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: n_weighted <dbl>, api_id <chr>
attr(ir, "bdhs_file")
#> [1] "BDIR81FL"
bdhs_read(2022, "IR", vars_regex = "^v1[0-9]{2}$", keep_design = FALSE, labels = "factor")
#> # A tibble: 22 × 5
#>    v106          v133 v130     v190       v191
#>    <fct>        <dbl> <fct>    <fct>     <dbl>
#>  1 primary          2 islam    poorer       99
#>  2 higher          14 islam    poorest  -34766
#>  3 primary          4 islam    richer    51054
#>  4 no education     0 islam    richer    50078
#>  5 primary          5 islam    richest  105222
#>  6 primary          5 islam    poorer    -9192
#>  7 higher          11 islam    richest  123568
#>  8 primary          2 islam    poorest -153754
#>  9 primary          4 islam    poorest  -52427
#> 10 primary          3 hinduism poorer     7740
#> # ℹ 12 more rows
#> ✔ Deleted the stored copy of "BD2022DHS IR".
#> ✔ Unregistered "BD2022DHS IR".
